core.title: Own each duplicated fragment once within its layer
core.given: two non-test production-source files of the same architectural layer share a run of 7 or more non-trivial lines that match after normalization (comments stripped; identifiers, strings and numbers folded, so renames don't hide it)
core.when: the repository-wide duplication scan reports the pair, whether the duplicate is newly introduced or pre-existing
core.then: Resolve it semantically: own one shared concept once within that layer, or make the real differences of two distinct responsibilities explicit.
prefer: Before extracting, check both share a responsibility and change reason, find the smallest stable shared behavior, and confirm it belongs in that layer.
For one concept, extract a focused function/module within the layer.
Name shared behavior by its domain or responsibility.
For different responsibilities, keep them independent and express real differences directly.
avoid: Renaming identifiers, changing literals, reordering harmless statements or other cosmetic edits to defeat normalization.
Cross-layer abstractions made just because layers hold similar-shaped code.
Highly parameterized generic helpers that obscure callers' intent.
Forcing distinct responsibilities into one abstraction to remove the finding.
A refactor that removes this finding but introduces new violations of the stack's conventions.
unless: Test artifacts, declaration-only files and re-export barrel files are excluded from the scan: the identifying patterns come from the stack's profile, and the exclusion itself is this rule's scan policy.
Files with no determinable layer are not judged.
core.why: A duplicate fingerprint is only a sensor that two sites MAY share one responsibility or change reason, so diagnose before extracting. The intra-layer limit is deliberate: twice in one layer is the shape that genuinely wants extracting; across layers it is usually two obligations, and merging couples layers that should move independently.
evidence: The duplication finding for the pair is gone after the change.
The duplicate was removed because ownership became clearer or because genuine semantic differences are now explicit — not via renames, literal changes or reordering.
Dependency direction and layer boundaries remain valid (no cross-layer abstraction introduced).
Any extracted abstraction has one coherent reason to change.
Existing behavior and tests remain green.
The refactor introduces no new violations of the stack's conventions (the stack's convention run after the change reports no new findings).
verification: Threshold: a run of 7 or more non-trivial normalized lines appearing in two different production-source files of the SAME architectural layer is a finding; comparison happens only within a layer.

Normalization per line: strip comments, fold string literals, numbers and non-keyword identifiers to placeholders, so renaming a variable cannot hide a duplicate and the fingerprint tracks STRUCTURE rather than text.
Trivial lines (bare braces, closing punctuation) are dropped and not counted toward the 7; every sliding window of 7 lines is fingerprinted and compared only within a layer.
Import and re-export declarations are not counted: two files importing the same names from one shared module match because the logic was shared, which is the fix this rule asks for.

Purely declarative shape-member signatures (fields of a type/interface-style body, including members of nested shapes) are not counted: unrelated records with the same number of same-typed fields match once identifiers are folded, and neither coupling them nor a cosmetic edit is a fix.
Executable statements, object literals, class fields, enum bodies and method bodies still count.

Scope: a repository-wide cross-file scan over every qualifying same-layer pair, whether newly introduced or pre-existing (strict, no baseline); it is not gated on which files the current diff touched. The scan excludes the file kinds identified positively by the stack's profile as test kinds, declaration-only files and re-export barrels (the exclusion itself is this rule's scan policy, not the profile's); files with undeterminable layer are not judged — with no established layer there is no intra-layer comparison, and unclassified paths are never compared with each other.

Enforcement: severity 2; disposition strict — every reported finding fails, including pre-existing ones; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. The check only reports structural duplication; the semantic diagnosis (one concept vs two responsibilities) is the agent's obligation, not the checker's.

fires: A run of 7+ non-trivial normalized lines in one domain-layer file also appears in another domain-layer file, even if variables were renamed and literals differ.
Two application-layer handlers share a run of 7+ non-trivial normalized executable lines differing only in identifiers and string literals.
A qualifying same-layer duplicate already existed before the current task and is untouched by the diff; the repository-wide scan still reports it.
doesNotFire: The same shape appears once in the domain layer and once in the presentation layer.
The match is in test artifacts, declaration-only files, or re-export barrel files.
The only matching lines are import/re-export declarations, bare braces/closing punctuation, or property/field signatures of declarative shape (type/interface-style) bodies.
One or both files cannot be assigned to a layer.
The duplicated run is shorter than 7 non-trivial normalized lines.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name patterns that identify the stack's declaration-only files (ambient/declaration type files with no executable code), so a rule can state its own policy over this file kind.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The suffix group's file_kind params (source, unit_test, acceptance_test, e2e_test, markup, plan_artifact, config) include no declaration-file kind, and no other group identifies this artifact kind; this rule's scan excludes it by rule policy, so other stack profiles need a key to supply the equivalent patterns.

proposedKeys.meaning: Name patterns that identify the stack's barrel files (re-export-only entry files), so a rule can state its own policy over this file kind.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The suffix group's file_kind params include no barrel/re-export kind, and no other group identifies this artifact kind; this rule's scan excludes barrels by rule policy, so other stack profiles need a key to supply the equivalent patterns.

neutralityNotes: The obligation, threshold (a run of 7 or more non-trivial normalized lines in two same-layer source files), strict no-baseline disposition and all prefer/avoid/evidence guidance are stack-neutral and kept in the core. Polarity note (audit round 2): the Bun sidecar encodes the scan's exclusion set as negated globs inside its activation fact; per the closed vocabulary the profile carries the POSITIVE patterns for each excluded kind, and the exclusion itself is stated by the core's scan policy (unless[0] and the scope verification entry). Round 3: the declaration-file and barrel patterns are no longer stranded in bunOnly — the newly proposed keys suffix.declaration_file (**/*.d.ts) and suffix.barrel (**/index.ts) carry them as profile data (alongside suffix.unit_test: **/*.test.*, **/*.spec.*, **/__tests__/**), while only the `!` negated-glob encoding remains bunOnly; roots.excluded is deliberately NOT used, since it denotes stack-wide vendored/generated trees, not this rule-specific scan exclusion. What could not be made neutral: the concrete normalization table tokens ('S', 0, ID) and the sha256-prefix fingerprint (detector mechanics, generalized to 'fold to placeholders' and 'structural fingerprint'); the TypeScript type/interface grammar for excluded property signatures (generalized to declarative shape-member signatures); and the detector/finding ids (bun_ts_metrics_detector, DUPLICATION-TS-001) plus the ATDD Bun ruleset framing (bunOnly per the notProfileKeys list; the core defers to the stack's convention runner via enforcement.runner).
